next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: GlassBox Anomaly Alerting: Real-Time Notifications and Automated Remediation
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: The integrity monitoring system now detects zero-token and low-token anomalies, but resolution is still manual. Build an automated remediation pipeline that: (1) Connects the /api/glassbox/integrity endpoint to a push-notification system (webhook, Slack, or local desktop notification via libnotify) so anomalies trigger an alert within 60 seconds of detection rather than waiting for a human to notice the dashboard badge; (2) Implements auto-remediation logic that, when a newly-completed mission is flagged as zero-token, automatically attempts rearchival via the rearchive_missions.py logic before the anomaly becomes a persistent record — reducing manual intervention to zero for the common case; (3) Adds an anomaly trend chart to the dashboard widget showing anomaly count over the last 30 days so operators can distinguish a one-off from a systematic regression; (4) Implements retention policy enforcement that archives anomalous mission manifests to a separate quarantine store with a 90-day TTL rather than leaving them in the main archive where they pollute integrity scan results; (5) Writes a chaos-engineering test harness that deliberately injects zero-token missions at known intervals and verifies the full pipeline (detection → alert → auto-remediation → verification) completes within a defined SLA (e.g., 120 seconds end-to-end). This turns the current passive monitoring system into an active self-healing infrastructure.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The current system excels at detection and visibility but requires manual intervention for resolution. The natural next step in any monitoring system lifecycle is automated remediation. The rearchive_missions.py script already provides the recovery primitive — wiring it to trigger automatically on anomaly detection (with appropriate guards against infinite loops) would make the token integrity guarantee self-enforcing. The chaos-engineering test harness would also serve as a regression guard for the remediation pipeline itself, ensuring the automation stays functional across future system changes.

final_report.summary: Built a complete automated token integrity monitoring system for GlassBox across 2 cycles. Cycle 1 delivered all 5 core components: (1) post-mission token sanity check integrated into the archival pipeline, (2) event schema validation in orchestrator.py's emit_mission_completed() to surface missing fields as warnings rather than silent zero-token archives, (3) a periodic health-check CLI script (token_integrity_check.py) scanning all mission archives for anomalously low token counts, (4) a REST endpoint GET /api/glassbox/integrity in dashboard_routes.py returning structured anomaly data, and (5) a regression test suite (test_token_integrity_pipeline.py) with 10 tests covering the full pipeline end-to-end. Cycle 2 applied the system to real historical data: ran the rearchive_missions.py recovery script (dry-run then live) against 10 identified zero-token missions, reducing confirmed anomalies to 2 genuine historical records (pre-token-logging era) plus expected test fixtures; and added an interactive integrity widget to the main AtlasForge dashboard (main_bundled.html) that polls /api/glassbox/integrity every 60 seconds, shows a color-coded badge (red when anomalies > 0, green when healthy), displays a stats grid (total scanned / normal / anomalous), and provides a collapsible list of anomalous mission IDs with dates and categories. All 10 regression tests pass (2.62s).

challenges_overcome: Historical zero-token missions with missing workspaces: rearchive script gracefully handled 'NO TRANSCRIPTS FOUND' cases where the original workspace no longer exists on disk, reporting them as irrecoverable rather than crashing

Distinguishing genuine anomalies from test fixtures: the integrity endpoint correctly categorizes test_synthetic_001, test_missing_workspace_002, and test_happy_path as expected fixtures, not production regressions
Dashboard widget integration without breaking existing layout: widget inserted into column 2 of the existing widget grid without CSS conflicts or JavaScript namespace collisions

JSONL token data absence for pre-logging-era missions: determined that missions before the token-logging infrastructure existed will always report zero tokens — flagged as expected historical data, not recoverable bugs
lessons_learned: Silent failures are more dangerous than noisy ones: the original zero-token archival bug accumulated across 3+ missions because nothing surfaced the error at the moment it occurred — always validate at write time, not just read time

Schema validation at event emission prevents cascading data corruption: adding mandatory field checks to emit_mission_completed() catches missing workspace paths before they propagate to the archive layer
Test fixtures must be clearly demarcated in anomaly detection: integrity scans should maintain an allowlist of expected fixture IDs to avoid false positives during regression test runs
Historical data recovery scripts should always have a --dry-run mode and report irrecoverable cases explicitly rather than silently skipping them
Dashboard widgets are highest-leverage observability tool: a single badge on the main dashboard provides more immediate feedback to operators than any background alert system
